title: General Grant's Whiskey: Results Over Rumors
summary: When temperance advocates complained that General Grant drank too much whiskey, Lincoln famously requested the brand name so he could send barrels to his other unsuccessful generals.
keywords: General Grant's Whiskey: Results Over Rumors
full_text:
In 1863, while Union generals in Virginia suffered demoralizing setbacks, General Ulysses S. Grant achieved spectacular victories in the western theater, capturing Fort Donelson and Vicksburg.

Jealous rivals and moralizing Washington politicians sought to sabotage Grant's standing. A delegation of temperance advocates and congressmen visited the White House:

"Mr. President! You must remove General Grant immediately! He is an unrepentant drunkard! He drinks whiskey constantly in his field tent! It is disgraceful that a drinking man leads Union troops!"

Lincoln leaned back in his rocking chair, listening with solemn attentiveness. He peered at the delegation leader:

"Gentlemen, this is grave intelligence. Do you have reliable witnesses who know the exact details of his consumption?"

"Yes, Mr. President! It is well known throughout the western camps!" they declared triumphantly.

Lincoln looked up, his face deadly serious:
"Then I have an urgent favor to ask of you gentlemen:
Can you inquire and find out for me the exact **brand of whiskey** that General Grant drinks?"

The delegates were utterly flabbergasted: "Why on earth would you need to know that, Mr. President?"

Lincoln slapped his desk with a hearty chuckle:
**"Because if I could find out, I should send a barrel of it to every other general in the field!
Perhaps then they might achieve a victory or two like Grant!"**

The self-righteous critics dispersed in silence.

Lincoln understood a profound truth of executive leadership: never sacrifice a battle-tested achiever to petty gossip and puritanical fault-finding.
moral: Judge people by their tangible achievements and loyalty in crisis, not by malicious rumors or minor personal eccentricities.
